answer: Give every identity a unique random data shard to guard, like a ridge of shale holding one fossil no other ridge shares. Each epoch the network fires unpredictable spot-checks at the shard, and only a holder at its zenith of readiness answers in time. A lone agent keeps one shard and passes cheaply. A farm must store a distinct shard per fake and answer spot-checks for all of them at once — storage and bandwidth costs scale linearly, shared shards are caught the moment two identities answer the same proof, and cloning earns nothing.
